Hi Jorge / Contracts team,

Thanks again for the productive review. Attached is our next pass (Redwood-OrderForm-v2.docx) with the limited redlines to try to keep the order form aligned with the MSA while addressing Acme's concerns. A few points we want to confirm before we circle back with legal: 

- Defense control: our standard is to reserve the right to assume defense for third-party IP claims but we are open to a defend-with-counsel compromise if Acme requires it.
- Subrogation/insurance: we can't accept a wholesale waiver of subrogation where it cuts across our insurers; propose standard insurance offset language instead.
- Evidence & notice: can you confirm the level of evidence Acme expects for a claim (proof-of-origin, sample prompts, logs)? we can provide a minimal evidence checklist but need ops involvement for anything beyond metadata.

If you can send back a redline or short note on those three items I can loop in legal and engineering for a quick call. Also note the HubSpot deal ID is HUBSPOT-76543.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Order form indemnity — evidence, subrogation & defense control discussion

Marissa —

Thanks for sending. Please see Acme's redlines attached (ACME-Redlines.pdf). Quick summary of our positions: 

1) Defense control: Acme will insist on the right to control defense for third-party IP claims (with counsel of our choosing) unless Redwood expressly assumes control. We can be flexible on settlement approval but need to preserve the right to direct.

2) Subrogation and insurance offsets: Acme is okay with Redwood's insurer stepping in, but we want a carveout that prevents Redwood from subrogating against Acme when Acme has paid a valid claim under its insurance; we will propose specific language.

3) Evidence threshold and retention: Acme requires a short evidence list (sample prompt, redacted user content, logs of model version + seed) and a 60-day preservation window after notice for us to validate.

We appreciate Redwood's willingness to compromise; can your legal team provide alternative language for defend-with-counsel and the proposed insurance waterfall? Also please confirm whether Redwood can commit to a 30-day notice window for non-emergency claims (we may need longer for some regulated lines).

Jorge —

Appreciate the clear positions. To move this forward and avoid a long back-and-forth, here's a pragmatic compromise we can offer from Redwood's side: 

- Defense control: Redwood will accept a "defend with counsel of Customer's choice" approach so long as Redwood retains final approval for settlements that would (i) impose ongoing obligations on Redwood, or (ii) create precedent-changing obligations. We can draft a short clause outlining settlement approval mechanics.

- Subrogation & insurance waterfall: we'll accept language that prevents Redwood from recovering twice on the same loss but cannot agree to an absolute bar on subrogation against Acme where Redwood's insurer has a valid claim. Proposed approach: insurance offset language + mutual subrogation carveouts for amounts actually paid by the other party's insurer.

- Evidence & retention: engineering (cc'd: Dylan) confirmed we can produce the evidence checklist below on a best-effort basis for the 60-day preservation window: model name + version, inference logs (timestamps + request IDs), redacted prompt sample, and a minimal KV cache snapshot where applicable. We'll need a legal hold/POC to gather anything beyond daily logs. I've attached a simple CSV template we use for evidence collection (evidence-template.csv).

Can your team accept those tradeoffs? If so, Kimberly (cc'd) will produce contract language and we can schedule a 30-minute call to finalize. Suggested times: Mon 6/29 10:00-11:00 PT or Tue 6/30 14:00-15:00 PT.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence-template.csv

Date: 2026-06-26T15:34:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Order form indemnity — evidence, subrogation & defense control discussion

Jorge / Acme Contracts —

Following up on Marissa's note. Redwood legal has drafted proposed language that implements the defend-with-counsel compromise and the insurance offset/subrogation approach described below. High level: 

- Settlement approval: Redwood must approve any settlement that would admit fault, impose ongoing obligations, or create affirmative obligations beyond monetary payment. If Redwood withholds approval reasonably, parties will engage in expedited escalation to resolve within 15 business days.
- Subrogation: mutual offset language; no double recovery; standard insurer step-in permitted; limited carveout where required by statute.
- Evidence & retention: we accept the 60-day preservation window for the listed artifacts. For forensic collection we will require a documented evidence request and a named POC for data pulls.

Attached is our proposed redline (Proposed-OrderForm-Redline.docx) that maps to the points above. Action items: 
1) Acme to review our redline and confirm acceptance or mark specific counterproposals (please use change-tracking).
2) If accepted in principle, schedule a short call (calendar link above) to agree on settlement approval mechanics and evidence POC.

Marissa will update the HubSpot record (HUBSPOT-76543) with the negotiation state. Ben — please prep an SOW addendum if Acme asks for longer-term preservation or enhanced logging retention. Dylan — please be on the call for technical Q&A.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
